_comment: Real sources for the Food Waste Reducer. No secrets. class_map keys = SOURCE labels; value = canonical taxonomy name, 'name:spoiled'/'name:fresh' to force freshness, or null to drop. Sources with "pending": true (or a missing root) are skipped by prepare_dataset.py (none pending now). 'max_per_class' caps images per class x freshness for 'folders' sources. Roots are outside the repo under mldata/. 'drop_image_if_label' drops an entire image if it contains any listed unmodelled object (so it is not left unlabeled). 'series_grouping': true groups numbered camera series (name_3, name_4, ...) into one split group; default is one group per original photo.

sources.name: vegqual
sources._note: Gourds are not taxonomy classes. 1615 of 4831 images are gourd-only (dropped automatically: no mapped boxes). 6 images mix gourds with other vegs; drop_image_if_label removes those so no gourd is left unlabeled.

sources.name: fridge_objects
sources._note: Roboflow v1, 963 images (train 731 / valid 125 / test 107), exported as yolov5pytorch (same YOLO txt layout). Names verified against data.yaml: avocado, bacon, butter, cheese, eggs, lemon, milk, pepper, tomatoes, yogurt. No freshness info: all boxes are assumed fresh (detector only, no classifier crops).

sources.name: hien_fridge
sources._note: Roboflow v12, 1,912 images (train 1378 / valid 363 / test 171), exported as yolov8. Names verified against data.yaml: apple, egg, milk_carton, others, soda_can, yogurt_container. 'others' is dropped (box only, image kept). All boxes assumed fresh.

sources.name: fresh_stale_fruits_veg
sources._note: Kaggle raghavrpotdar/fresh-and-stale-images-of-fruits-and-vegetables, CC0 1.0, folder-per-class, 14,683 files (fresh_/stale_ x apple, banana, bitter_gourd, capsicum, orange, tomato). stale -> spoiled, capsicum -> bell_pepper, bitter_gourd dropped (whole image; not a taxonomy class, bitter_melon comes in a later PR). Files are augmentations ('name.jpg_0_1039.jpg') of far fewer originals and are grouped by original name; 'Screen Shot <date> at <time>' names give capture times. max_per_class=250 caps images per class x freshness (after the cap about 2,500 images, so it does not swamp VegQual 3.2k / fridge 2.9k).
sources.version_note: Kaggle dataset; no version number exposed (record download date 2026-10-10).

sources.name: agrifreshnet
sources._note: AgriFreshNET (Mendeley Data v1, doi 10.17632/42m5tb7yv9.1, CC BY 4.0): 8 produce x Fresh/Semi fresh/Rotten, 590 images per folder, HEAVILY AUGMENTED (about 92% of images have a flip/rotation-aware pHash<=6 near-duplicate in their own class). Staged by `python -m pipeline ingest-dataset` with PIPELINE_SPECIMEN_GROUPS=1: the staged name is `<class>__spec_<id>.rf.<sha>_<orig stem>.jpg`, where <id> is a cross-stage component of 8-variant pHash distance (<=10, tightened to 6/4 per class when one component exceeded 30%), so prepare_dataset keeps every specimen and its augmentations in one split. semi_fresh is kept as its own label. Classification crops only (no boxes): whole image = one object.

sources.name: meatscan
sources._note: MeatScan (Zenodo 16764338, CC BY 4.0; Data in Brief 2025 doi:10.1016/j.dib.2025.112045): raw cow meat, fresh/spoiled, phone photos from two Kumasi markets, 14-16 Feb 2024. 6,995 originals + 4,005 author augmentations in one 25.4 GB RAR. Fetched by HTTP range reads of ORIGINALS only (python -m pipeline fetch-meatscan, 450 per class spread over date x market x hour), then ingested with --adapter meatscan --max-per-cell 300: capture time from MeatScan_Metadata.csv goes into the staged name so the 300 s session split applies. Whole-frame boxes (single-subject photos). First non-produce freshness source (ML-16).

sources.name: dafif
sources._note: DaFiF (Mendeley vx4ptwk3pb v1, CC BY 4.0; Data in Brief 57 (2024) 111016): mackerel, tilapia, tuna on ice for 11 days, 10 fish per species, two sessions a day. No image freshness labels in the release: labelled by storage day per the data owner's rule (2026-10-10): days 1-3 fresh, days 9-11 spoiled, days 4-8 dropped. Fetched with python -m pipeline fetch-dafif (300 per freshness, round-robin over species x session x day, SHA-256 checked, downscaled to 1280 px); ingested with --adapter dafif, which groups by species + session across days (the same fish) so a batch never straddles splits. Whole-frame boxes.

sources.name: food_hvk7g
sources._note: PENDING, not downloadable as published (checked 2026-10-10 with the private key): the project has 0 generated versions, and Roboflow only serves a generated version (only its owner can generate one). Classes are '2', 'orange', 'oranges', 'Platano' (696 images, object detection), with NO freshness labels, so even if forked it can only teach the detector banana/orange (assumed fresh is wrong for a set described as including spoiled food). To use it: fork it into our Roboflow workspace (Universe -> Fork Project), generate a version, then map Platano->banana, orange(s)->orange, drop '2', and hand-label freshness or keep it detector-only with freshness excluded from metrics.

sources.name: food_spoilage_status
sources._note: Roboflow 'Food Spoilage Status' (workspace food-monitoring), v1, 276 images (train 193 / valid 55 / test 28), instance segmentation: the yolov8 export has POLYGON labels, which prepare_dataset.yolo_line_to_box turns into enclosing boxes. Names verified against data.yaml 2026-10-10 (12 classes): fresh/spoiled x apple, banana, capsicum, orange, potato, bitter gourd. File names carry capture times (20190809_165458_jpg.rf.<hash>), so the 300 s session split applies. Added at the data owner's request.
